responsibilities: Build and own the test infrastructure that makes AMR acceptance testing repeatable across every MAG variant and hardware generation.
Run the released Botsync Artifact through independent, full-stack hardware-and-software verification before sign-off - commissioning-grade rigor applied in the lab, before it ever reaches a site.

Test infrastructure, end to end - Design, build, and maintain HIL rigs and physical test fixtures spanning every MAG AMR variant (lifter, forklift, counterbalance, conveyor, tugger) and hardware generation (R2/R3/new), so acceptance runs are repeatable, not improvised per release.

Deployment-profile automation - Build and own the automation that runs deployment-profile gates per site/variant/generation against the release candidate, replacing manual bench-testing with a repeatable regression pass.

Full-stack acceptance testing - Run the released candidate through hardware-level acceptance tests before sign-off, exercising hardware, firmware, and software together the way a commissioning engineer would on a live site - not layer by layer in isolation.

Independent verification, not build - Test and certify robot behavior across variants and generations without owning or patching the production robot software or hardware under test; defects go back to the owning Robotics team, never fixed in place.

Defect triage and traceability - Log, reproduce, and route hardware-surfaced defects to the correct Robotics or SyncOS team with enough rig data, logs, and repro steps to unblock a fix without back-and-forth.
